articles.title: Was Benjamin Franklin the original wellness bro? I lived like him for a day to find out
articles.description: Before online influencers existed, the founding father published an annual wellness pamphlet. I followed his 13 virtues he found necessary for a good life Benjamin Franklin doesn’t get enough credit. Yes, he was a founding father of the United States; he invented the lightning rod and his face is printed on $100 bills. But rarely is he celebrated for his contributions to the most meaningful field of human achievement: wellness influencing. Centuries before GRWM videos and scientifically dubious podcasts were a dollar-sign-shaped glint in their creators’ eyes, Franklin was doling out life advice. Under the pseudonym Poor Richard, Franklin published an annual pamphlet and minted maxims like “Diligence is the mother of good luck” and “Fish and visitors stink after three days.” Continue reading...
